why: Runner-minute budget for the e2e gate's Playwright work per PR head and per queue draft
(TEST-BUDGET round 3, Fri 30 Oct 2026; the maintainer's design change the same day: a HARD cap of 10
runner minutes per run across pytest, e2e and the fixed jobs, of which the e2e share on a
frontend PR is about 4). scripts/ci_e2e_selection.py prices its selection with the model
below and takes the best-ranked root specs and named gates until the budget is spent;
what it drops is listed under `budget` in e2e-selection.json so an escape can be attributed.
JSON, not YAML, because the scope job runs on the runner's bare python3 (no PyYAML);
the shape mirrors ci/test-budget.yml (round 0). Decision record:

comment: planned minutes = root_overhead_min + root spec seconds / 60 * min_per_recorded_minute
+ per kept named gate: gate_overhead_min + its recorded seconds / 60 * min_per_recorded_minute.
Overheads are the engine and Vite boots the step pays before its first test; the recorded
seconds come from the footprint map, measured on the host that built it. Both overheads
are first estimates from the gate's logs (root boot about 60 s, a gate's own engine about
30 s) and are the next thing to fit on real runs.
Estimated runner minutes per named gate that has no footprint and no recorded seconds
(production builds, a no-server spec, a shell script), so an unmeasured gate is never
free to the budget. First estimates from gate job logs, to be replaced by measurement.

rank: overlap: the number of changed files the spec or gate executed, descending
seconds: the spec's or gate's recorded seconds, ascending
unmeasured specs and gates rank after every overlap
